CTRL + AI: Playing with Intelligence
media:group.media:description:
CTRL + AI: Playing with Intelligence brings together Eldad Tsabary and Scott DeJong for a participatory conversation about what games and simulated worlds can reveal about artificial intelligence and about us.
Tsabary’s Village is a persistent AI world populated by characters who remember, develop relationships, acquire expertise and continue interacting when the user/creator is absent. What began as an attempt to create one convincing artificial person grew into an evolving social environment and a mirror for examining memory, identity, conflict, trust and the subtle behaviours that make an interaction feel human, or strangely alien.
DeJong approaches related questions through games and public participation. His projects use play to make AI ethics, media bias and information systems tangible: not to tell participants what is right or wrong, but to help them examine how they use AI, what they trust, and how individual choices connect to broader social consequences.
Moderated by Christian Beltrami, the conversation will bring these two approaches together. What happens when an AI world and a human audience confront the same questions about knowledge, fear, agency and the future? How do we know when an artificial expert deserves our trust? Can play help us think critically about AI without reducing the discussion to either enthusiasm or rejection?
Through conversation, audience prompts and game elements, the event invites participants to explore AI not as a technological spectacle, but as a tool for asking better questions about human intelligence, relationships and responsibility.

media:group.media:title: Climate Leadership Story Hub
media:group.media:description:
Montréal Climate Week Flagship Event
Join us for a screening of ᑰᒃ ᑰᑦᑐᖅ The Flowing River, a short documentary that returns to Inukjuak after the community's hydro facility is complete. Inukjuak is leading one of the largest clean-energy transitions in the Arctic.
The screening will be followed by a discussion among community partners Sarah Lisa Kasudluak, Eric Atagotaaluk, and Tommy Palliser, as well as one of Canada’s foremost energy transition commentators, Chris Henderson — all featured in the documentary — and the founder and director of the Climate Leadership Story Hub, Aphrodite Salas.
There will also be a photo gallery display of photos taken by Lina Forero during the making of the documentary.

media:group.media:title: Future Genders Archive
media:group.media:description:
What if artificial intelligence didn’t constrain, categorize, or define us, but instead opened up infinite possibilities for how we express our gender and identify?
The Future Genders Archive is a workshop series that uses speculative design and zine-making as tools of radical imagination. Join us for our program launch event to explore alternative technological worlds, learn more about the project, and create your own speculative zine artifact!
The Agenda:
Lindsay Rodgers + Jennifer Addison: Introduce Future Genders Archive workshop series + lead facilitators Casey Burkholder: Crafting as Community Building
IN PERSON ONLY Le Lin: Zine-making workshop

media:group.media:title: Grad School Myths, Busted
media:group.media:description:
Think graduate school is only for future professors? Worried it might be too expensive, too isolating, or only for students who already have everything figured out?
Join Concordia Graduate Student Ambassadors for an honest panel that tackles some of the most common myths about grad school. Students will share what they wish they had known earlier, how they made their decision, and what graduate studies actually look like once you begin. You’ll hear real perspectives on workload, funding, research and course-based programs, English-language study, finding community, and how grad school can support different academic and career goals.

media:group.media:title: Meet & Geek! - Podcast!
media:group.media:description:
Meet & Geek is a collaborative event bringing together Concordia Game Development and the Concordia Esports Students Association for a day of games, demos, and conversations around game development and gaming culture.
During the event, attendees will have the opportunity to explore and play a selection of student-made games, ranging from indie titles and VR experiences to 1v1 challenges featuring some of the most popular games. The afternoon will feature introductions and a Q&A session, giving attendees the opportunity to connect with the people behind the projects, ask questions, and learn more about game development at Concordia. We will also be presenting a special exhibition from Space Cast Magazine, so attendees can keep an eye out for some spacey art!

media:group.media:description:
Join us for an insightful discussion featuring Daniel Rowland. With over 17 billion streams, Daniel is a music producer and tech executive at LANDR. His extensive career includes work with major entities like Pixar and Disney, and artists such as Nine Inch Nails, Eminem, and Nina Simone.

entry.title: MORE THAN MUSIC: Building a Brand People Remember

media:group.media:title: MORE THAN MUSIC: Building a Brand People Remember
media:group.media:description:
Join us for a conversation on what it takes to build a career that extends beyond the music itself.
Featuring former Dim Mak President Lorne Padman, Turn Muzik VP of A&R Charles Lewis, and DJ & tastemaker/curator Grahm Radio, this session explores how artists can stand out in a crowded industry by building a memorable brand and meaningful relationships.
We'll discuss authentic networking, approaching labels and managers professionally, and turning connections into long-term opportunities.
About the Speakers:
Dr. Sunni is a performance psychologist, consultant, and executive coach. She is the host of Psych Drop, a podcast exploring the psychology of success in electronic dance music through conversations with artists, managers, and industry leaders. Also known as The Psychologist Beyond the Booth, she helps artists and music industry professionals develop the mindset, leadership, and decision-making skills needed to navigate pressure, build meaningful careers, and sustain long-term success. Dr. Sunni brings more than two decades of experience in psychology and leadership development, offering a practical perspective on the human side of building a career in electronic music.
